title: Riverside Pricing 2026: Free, Pro and Grow Plans
summary: Riverside pricing ranges from free to $39 monthly, with costs varying by plan and payment frequency.

## Automate Riverside recordings with Activepieces


It won't lower what you pay Riverside, but if the connector for your post-session chores is missing, Activepieces lets you generate it with AI and add it privately to your own instance, with no vendor release to wait for.


Roughly 60% of its 747 integrations were contributed by the community, and you can count them in the open source monorepo.


Activepieces is an MIT-licensed automation platform that connects the apps you already use, so one event in one app sets off actions in others, and it does that across 747 integrations without limiting you on flows: every plan, including free, has unlimited flows.


### What a Riverside post-recording workflow does


Left alone, a finished recording sits in Riverside until someone remembers to download it, rename it, drop it in the right folder and tell the editor.


When that someone is you, the cost is the time you spend on it and the days a file waits because nobody was told it existed.


Put a workflow in place of that memory and you have a fixed routine. Here's the sequence worth building, in the order it runs:


1. Trigger when a Riverside recording finishes, so the routine starts without anyone clicking anything.
2. File the recording and its transcript to your storage, in a folder named the same way every time.
3. Create a task for the editor, with a link to the files, so the handoff is written down instead of remembered.
4. Post a notification to the team channel, so the team knows the episode is ready.


The routine is only as good as step one. Before you build anything, check inside Activepieces that it can see a finished Riverside recording and reach the transcript. If it can't, the rest has nothing to start from.


### When Riverside automation isn't worth the effort


If you record rarely, the chores take a few minutes and a workflow takes longer to set up and check than it'll ever save.


The same goes for a solo creator who edits their own files: there's no handoff to automate, and a task assigned to yourself is clutter.


It also does nothing for the problems that decide which Riverside plan you buy, such as hours of recording, export limits and seats. Those come from the plan, not from what happens afterward.


Finally, an automation is one more thing that can break quietly. If nobody will notice a missing file or a silent notification, you've swapped a visible chore for a hidden risk. Build it when several people depend on the handoff, not before.
